newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: S.Leone coup makers seek 18 months in power. [CORRECTED 00:15 GMT 6/6]
newsitem.headline: S.Leone coup makers seek 18 months in power. [CORRECTED 00:15 GMT 6/6]

text.p: (Corrects headline from "said to seek 10 months in power")

Sierra Leone's coup makers seek 18 months (corrects from 10 months) of power before handing over to an interim body to steer the war-torn West African nation to fresh elections, politicians invited for talks with them said on Thursday.
The politicians, who included members of ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah's administration and members of the opposition, said they rejected the suggestion outright.

Regional power Nigeria, acting in the name of Sierra Leone's West African neighbours, has troops in Freetown to press the coup leaders to reinstate Kabbah who was deposed by junior officers on May 25.

On Monday, Nigerian gunboats shelled the city and their forces clashed with dissident Sierra Leone soldiers and their rebel allies, who took up arms in 1991 and have flooded into the capital since the coup.

State radio reported that the coup leader, Major Johnny Paul Koromah, had held talks with a Nigerian delegation which assured them that Nigerian forces had no further plans to attack military bases in the city and would not intervene further.
The politicians dismissed the radio report as propaganda. Nigeria, which already had troops in the city under a defence agreement, has been steadily reinforcing.
The politicians said a Ghanaian delegation, in town to try to broker a peaceful end to the standoff, would meet Koromah later on Thursday.

Kabbah won 1996 elections which ended four years of military rule in Sierra Leone -- one of the world's poorest nations despite its mineral riches. The latest military coup was the third in five years.
